mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 1.00% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.00% in a month
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative during high-rate months, or FEDFUNDS spikes fail to precede negative SPX 20d returns with statistically significant negative IC (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 5.5% for two consecutive months is associated with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as rising labor market rigidity reduces corporate investment demand.
regime_hint: Rising unemployment and tightening labor market
failure_condition: In regimes with low inflation, UNRATE exceeds 5.5% for two months but SPX 60d returns are not statistically different from zero (IC > 0.05), or the effect reverses in high-inflation periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in HOUST (units of new orders) of at least 10% coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as weak order flow signals reduced risk appetite and equity discounting.
failure_condition: During periods of high inflation, HOUST declines ≥10% but SPX 20d returns are not statistically positive (IC > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly reading of INDPRO above 102.0 (2017=100) while CPIAUCSL is flat or rising indicates a supply-side expansion that compresses SPX forward discounting, producing a positive 5-day return.
failure_condition: Over 12 months, this pattern recurs but SPX 5d returns remain negative on average (IC < -0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in GDPC1 (real private consumption) by at least 3% in a quarter coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as reduced consumption growth lowers equity growth expectations.
failure_condition: In contraction quarters with falling CPIAUCSL, GDPC1 < -3% but SPX 20d returns are not statistically negative (IC > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When PAYEMS rises by more than 10,000 in a month while UNRATE remains below 4%, it signals a strengthening labor market that supports corporate optimism and a positive 60-day SPX forward return.
regime_hint: Labor market strengthening without inflationary pressure
failure_condition: Across 24 months, this pattern recurs but 60d SPX returns are not significantly higher than baseline (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 5% predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to reduced consumer confidence and equity discounting.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls ≥5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In high-growth regimes, RSAFS declines ≥5% but SPX 20d returns are not statistically negative (IC > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly convergence of INDPRO and HOUST to their 12-month moving averages signals easing supply constraints and a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as market pricing in supply normalization.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST converge to their respective 12mo moving averages in a month
failure_condition: Over 6 months, this convergence occurs but 60d SPX returns are not statistically positive (IC < 0.05).
